:::{#thm-hadamard-local-decoding}
#### Two-query decoding of the Hadamard code

Let $w$ be a binary string of length $2^k$,
with $w(a)$ its symbol at the position indexed by $a \in \ffield{2}^k$,
that differs from the [Hadamard codeword](#def-hadamard-code) of $x$
in at most a fraction $\errfrac$ of its positions.
Fix $i \in \set{1, \ldots, k}$,
and let $e_i$ have a 1 in position $i$ only.
Choose $a \in \ffield{2}^k$ [uniformly at random](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-uniform) and output $w(a) + w(a + e_i) \pmod 2$.
The output equals $x_i$ with [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) at least $1 - 2\errfrac$.

:::

::: {.proof}
Both $a$ and $a + e_i$ are [uniformly distributed](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-uniform) on $\ffield{2}^k$,
so each of $w(a)$ and $w(a + e_i)$ is wrong with [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) at most $\errfrac$,
and the chance that either is wrong is at most $2\errfrac$,
so both are correct with probability at least $1 - 2\errfrac$.
When both are correct, the output is

$$\dprod{x}{a} + \dprod{x}{\paren{a + e_i}} = \dprod{x}{e_i} = x_i,$$

because $\dprod{x}{a} + \dprod{x}{a} = 0$ modulo 2.

:::
